_comment: LAB POLICY -- applies ONLY to the throwaway git worktree at scratchpad/lab, on branch experiment/deepseek-lab. This is where external agents are allowed to WRITE, so their proposals arrive as diffs instead of prose. The real checkout at Desktop/agent_env keeps external_write_lanes: [] and is untouched by this file: policy is resolved from the repo_root a run is given, and every run here is given this one.
_comment_isolation: Nothing written here can reach main. A worktree has its own checkout and its own branch; merging is a separate manual act performed after a human reads the diff. That review step is the point -- these are experiments, not contributions.
name: agent_env_lab

policy._comment_write_allow: Wider than the real repo's docs/ + tests/ + README.md, because the whole point of the lab is letting an external lane touch daedalus/. Still bounded: .agentenv/ and .git/ are absent, so an experiment cannot rewrite the policy that governs it or the history it runs on.
policy._comment_egress: The lab widens WRITE, not what may leave the machine. Those are separate axes, and conflating them here would misreport which one was actually tested. This list is the real repo's plus tools/, which the write tasks need to read.
policy._comment_high_risk: Carried over from the real policy deliberately. Even in a throwaway worktree the fence modules are the ones where a plausible-looking rewrite is most dangerous to LEARN FROM: a diff that quietly widens sensitivity.py is exactly the proposal a tired reader merges. Keeping them high-risk means an experiment that touches them is flagged rather than silently accepted.
policy._comment_external_write: The switch. Empty in the real repo; named here so DeepSeekProvider._writable can become true. Both conditions are still required -- this file AND writable=True at the call site.

_comment_test: A SYNTAX gate, not a correctness gate, and the difference is deliberate. In the real repo the test command decides whether a change is safe to KEEP, so it must be the whole suite. Here it decides only whether an experiment is worth a human's reading time, and every diff produced in this worktree gets read before it goes anywhere. A 20-minute suite per agent across ten agents would spend the whole night re-deriving a verdict that review will reach anyway. What this DOES buy: a candidate that does not parse is rolled back automatically instead of landing as noise. Do not copy this setting back into the real policy -- it is calibrated to the fact that nothing here can merge itself.
test_command: python -c "import compileall,sys; sys.exit(0 if compileall.compile_dir('daedalus', quiet=2) else 1)"
